subject: Urban Planning
title: The Gas Tax Problem
description: A quick win: understand The Gas Tax Problem.

hook.text: America's roads are funded by gas taxes. As cars go electric, the money is disappearing.

buildup.text: The federal gas tax hasn't been raised since 1993. Inflation has eaten 40% of its value.

discovery.text: Electric cars pay no gas tax but cause the same road wear. The funding model is collapsing.

twist.text: Some states are testing mileage-based fees: pay per mile driven, not per gallon bought.

climax.text: The shift from gas tax to mileage fee will reshape how America thinks about driving costs.

punchline.text: Electric cars fix emissions. They break the road budget.

quiz.question: Why is America's gas tax becoming insufficient?
options: Oil companies are lobbying to eliminate it entirely
Electric cars pay no gas tax and the rate hasn't risen since 1993
More people are working from home and driving less
